    AI anxiety: 5 ways to cope when you’re scared of AI

    📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that if you’re feeling a mix of emotions about artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and how they’re shaping our world, you’re not alone.
    • Industry observers note that AI anxiety is the worry or unease some people feel about the fast growth of artificial intelligence and how quickly technology is changing.
    • According to recent reports, AI research goes back decades, but progress has sped up sharply in recent years with the arrival of chatbots, AI image generators, and other tools.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that if you’re feeling a mix of emotions about artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and how they’re shaping our world, you’re not alone. Chief Clinical Officer at Calm, Chris Mosunic, PhD, has tips and strategies to help tame a growing source of anxiety.

    Industry observers note that AI anxiety is the worry or unease some people feel about the fast growth of artificial intelligence and how quickly technology is changing. It isn’t a clinical diagnosis, but the feelings are real and common. They can focus on everyday risks, such as job loss and AI-powered scams, and bigger ones, such as AI getting out of human control.

    According to recent reports, AI research goes back decades, but progress has sped up sharply in recent years with the arrival of chatbots, AI image generators, and other tools. A 2023 Calm survey* found that nearly 1 in 3 U.S. adults (29%) felt anxious about AI, and 18% described their feelings as fear or dread. At the same time, 31% felt optimistic, and 31% felt excited. Many respondents felt a mix: amazed by AI and nervous about it.

    In a recent development, concern about AI has stayed high in the years since. In a June 2026 Pew Research Center survey, 52% of U.S. adults noted they feel more concerned than excited about AI in daily life. That’s up from 37% in 2021 and about the same as in 2023. Just 9% said they feel more excited than concerned.

    It has been revealed that it’s hard to know how AI will affect our safety and our lives. You might wonder how it will change your job, what it could mean for areas like scientific research, and what the future will look like. Many of us find uncertainty hard to cope with, so feeling anxious or out of control is understandable. But when anxiety feels overwhelming, it can start to affect your sleep, mood, and focus.

    These five ways to manage AI anxiety draw on mindfulness and common thinking traps, like catastrophizing. Start with whichever fits how you feel today.

    The rapid rise in AI and automation can feel like a threat to our livelihoods (and even our lives), making many of us feel unstable and out of control.

    In a recent development, resist resisting: When confronted with uncertainty, our first instinct can often be to fight it. Try sitting with it instead. Notice how the discomfort shows up in your body and mind.

    Go at your own pace: Give yourself time to adjust to the fresh realities of AI.

    Talk it out: Process your anxieties with a friend or a coworker. You may find someone who feels the same way.

    💙 On those days when you feel overwhelmed by the rapidly changing tech landscape, try a simple meditation practice like Pause to Breathe to help you feel more grounded.

    If you’re feeling anxious or uneasy about AI, don’t invalidate or try to avoid those emotions — that approach can make things worse. Instead, let yourself feel anxious. Telling yourself you’re overreacting can damage your self-trust and self-confidence.

    According to recent reports, identify the emotions: Get a better understanding of what you’re feeling. Your anxiety could mean you’re working through a more deeply rooted problem, like feeling threatened or inadequate.

    Try meditation: Meditation can help you ground yourself in the present moment and tune into what you’re feeling and where it’s coming from.

    Write down all your anxieties without censoring yourself: Set aside dedicated time each day to think through your anxious thoughts, helping you process and make sense of your emotions.

    💙 Take some time to stop and do this short Emotions Check-In to make space for any anxious feelings.

    Industry observers note that when we’re feeling anxious about the unknown, many of us fall into the trap of catastrophic thinking, imagining the worst possible outcome, even without evidence to support it. This can cause low-level anxieties to spiral out of control.

    Challenge your worst fears: What evidence do you have that they’re true or that they’ll happen?

    In a recent development, bring to mind times in the past that felt groundbreaking in the tech world: Think back to the creation of mobile phones, laptops, or even navigation apps, and consider how you’ve adapted to their existence despite any initial anxieties or concerns. The same could happen with AI.

    Bring your mind back to the now: The future feels a whole lot less intimidating when you focus on the present.

    💙 One of the best ways you can bring yourself back to the present is through mindfulness meditation, which you can learn in the Mindfulness for Beginners series.

    Many of us find ourselves viewing situations as an all-or-nothing approach. This is a cognitive distortion called polarized thinking, and it often occurs because we’re focused on the extremes without considering the nuances or possibilities of any given situation.

    The debate around AI is nuanced. Popular culture shows dystopian futures, so it can be easy to think there’s only one possible outcome with AI.

    In a recent development, however, reality tends to exist in between the extremes, so remind yourself that it’s perfectly normal for opposing emotions or views to be present at the same time. And they can also all feel as strong, real, or true as each other. You can feel fascinated and terrified, anxious and excited, or resentful and grateful.

    When we allow multiple truths to co-exist in our minds, we make space for more ease. So try to hold space for the contradictions and the possibilities.

    💙 For a more in-depth discussion on how to use mindfulness to combat worrying and keep nuance at the forefront, check out the Overcome Stress & Anxiety series.

    In a recent development, at the extreme end of AI anxiety, some of us may have a deep—even subconscious—fear about a machine taking over. We ask questions like: Is this the beginning of the end of humanity? Will humans be replaced by robots?

    Sources indicate that A fear of overdependence on technology can cause us to worry about the negative consequences of relying too heavily on artificial intelligence. One way to remedy this fear is to embrace our humanity.

    Be present for the little things you often take for granted, like hugs, laughing until it hurts, or exchanging a look with your best friend.

    Make time for the people in your life, and prioritize connecting with them face-to-face when you can.

    Marvel at the awesomeness of human things like awkward silences or goosebumps when you’re listening to music.

    Ask people how they’re really feeling and practice deep listening when they respond.

    Disconnect from technology and spend time in nature.

    💙 Embrace the power of being human and living in the now by reading a book, listening to a meditation, or taking a Mindful Walk.

    *Calm research was fielded among n = 450 adults in the US between March 21, 2023 and March 22, 2023 and is nationally representative, with quotas across age, gender, race, ethnicity, and region.

    In a recent development, recent news stories have shown how general-purpose AI tools may respond in unsafe or harmful ways, especially when people are vulnerable or struggling with a mental health crisis. These situations are rare, but they highlight an important truth: AI is not human and can’t accurately recognize risk, provide crisis support, or understand the complexity of your emotional world.

    Sources indicate that AI can support mental health — especially when it’s part of a program designed and guided by licensed professionals. But general AI tools, like chatbots or large language models, are not a replacement for real human care.

    If you’re struggling, please consider reaching out to a therapist or support line — many offer free or low-cost options. You deserve support that’s personal, thoughtful, and real.

    In a recent development, U.S. - Call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

    Worldwide - Visit findahelpline.com for free, confidential resources.

    Your mental health matters and you don’t have to navigate tough moments alone.

    To manage anxiety about artificial intelligence, there are proactive steps you can take.

    Educate yourself about AI to understand its capabilities and limitations better: Learning about AI can make it feel less intimidating.

    Engage in conversations about AI: Talking with others about your concerns can offer upcoming perspectives and reduce feelings of isolation.

    Practice mindfulness and stress-reduction techniques: Managing your anxiety effectively can help you focus on the present and reduce worries about the future.

    Stay informed about AI developments: Understand how it's being integrated into society to help you feel more prepared and less anxious.

    According to recent reports, fear of artificial intelligence is common and can stem from several concerns, such as uncertainty about how AI will affect the future, including potential changes in the job market and societal norms. You may also have concerns about privacy, security, and the ethical use of AI. The idea of losing control to machines or facing decisions made by algorithms without empathy can be daunting.

    Understanding these fears and addressing them through education and dialogue can help alleviate the anxiety associated with AI.

    Sources indicate that you don’t have to be, though some concern is understandable. AI is changing fast, and it raises real questions, from job loss and scams to whether people can keep control of it. Some risks deserve attention. Others are far from certain, and no one knows exactly how AI will unfold. When we’re anxious, our minds jump to the worst outcome and can treat every headline as proof of a disastrous future.

    Industry observers note that it can help to follow reliable news sources and take breaks from stories that leave you on edge. When your thoughts race ahead, try a mindfulness practice to bring your attention back to today. If worry about AI is getting in the way of sleep or daily life, consider talking with a therapist or doctor.

    The fear of AI doesn’t have a widely recognized specific term but is often considered a form of “technophobia,” which is the fear of advanced technology or complex devices. When this fear centers on AI, it can stem from concerns that the technology could surpass human intelligence and from the ethical consequences of machines making decisions that affect people’s lives. AI anxiety is rooted in the unknown future impact of AI on humanity.

    While AI offers many benefits, concerns about its negative effects remain. These include potential job losses due to automation, as AI can perform some tasks more efficiently than humans. Privacy issues are also a significant concern, as AI systems can process vast amounts of personal data, sometimes without clear consent or transparency. Security risks may arise if AI systems are hacked or malfunction. AI can also perpetuate bias if its training data is biased, leading to unfair or unethical decisions.

    On a societal level, increased reliance on AI could reduce human interaction and erode certain skills as machines take over more tasks. Understanding these potential negative effects can help develop strategies to mitigate them and ensure AI is used responsibly and ethically.

    It has been revealed that mental health is hard. Getting support doesn't have to be. The Calm app puts the tools to feel better in your back pocket, with personalized content to manage stress and anxiety, get better sleep, and feel more present in your life.

    #22897. Breaking: This Chain Was Dunkin's Bitter Rival In The '50s — Now It's The Most Popular Donut Spot In Japan

    📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (606 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: This Chain Was Dunkin's Bitter Rival In The '50s — Now It's The Most Popular Donut Spot In Japan

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that dunkin' is one of America's favorite spots to grab a quick donut and one of its famous syrup-infused iced coffees — which we ranked from worst to best.
    • It has been revealed that what makes this feud particularly fascinating is that it was a family affair.
    • Industry observers note that as is often the case, feuds rarely end with a clear winner.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that dunkin' is one of America's favorite spots to grab a quick donut and one of its famous syrup-infused iced coffees — which we ranked from worst to best. Today, the chain boasts more than 10,000 stores in the U.S. alone and sits comfortably at the top of the country's donut hierarchy. However, it wasn't always the undisputed heavyweight. In a rivalry that gives McDonald's and Burger King a run for their money, Dunkin' spent decades going head-to-head with Mister Donut. Ultimately, Dunkin' came out on top — at least, if we're talking strictly about the USA. Over in Japan, Mister Donut reigns supreme.

    It has been revealed that what makes this feud particularly fascinating is that it was a family affair. Dunkin', originally known as Dunkin' Donuts, was founded in 1950 by William Rosenberg. The simple combination of donuts and coffee proved to be a huge success. Naturally, Rosenberg wanted to expand the business through franchising. So far, so good, right? Well, not everyone was happy with the idea, including Harry Winokur, Rosenberg's brother-in-law. In a move that would spark a decades-long rivalry, Winokur left the business and opened Mister Donut just a few miles from Dunkin's original location. He even embraced franchising, with Mister Donut employees reportedly being prohibited from saying the word "dunk" in their stores.

    Industry observers note that as is often the case, feuds rarely end with a clear winner. In 1990, Dunkin' acquired Mister Donut and rebranded nearly all of its American locations as Dunkin' stores (ouch). Today, just one Mister Donut location remains in the U.S. That must have been a hit on Winokur's pride, but while Dunkin' was busy making cereal in the '80s, Mister Donut was thriving on the other side of the world. Today, Mister Donut is Japan's leading donut chain, with more than 900 locations in operation.

    Sources indicate that japan has embraced plenty of Western-style foods with open arms. Think of the juicy, hamburger-inspired hambāgu, or comforting pizza toast with its wide array of toppings. Mister Donut also happens to fit comfortably into this category. However, one thing worth knowing about Japan's take on Western staples is that they're rarely direct copies. Instead, the country has a knack for putting its own spin on imported dishes. That's exactly how Mister Donut managed to carve out a place for itself in the market.

    The first Mister Donut opened its doors in Japan in 1971, after business executive Seiichi Suzuki acquired the exclusive rights to operate the brand in the country. The original menu featured familiar American favorites, but Suzuki also introduced items and adjustments designed to appeal to local tastes. These included reducing the sugar content of certain products, serving more modest portions, and creating a cozy, sit-down atmosphere. The approach proved successful, and Mister Donut quickly expanded across Japan. Dunkin', meanwhile, had also tried its luck in the Japanese market, opening its first location in 1970. While Mister Donut continued to grow, Dunkin' struggled to gain a foothold and eventually left Japan altogether in 1998.

    In 1989, Suzuki's manufacturer Duskin acquired full ownership of Mister Donut's Japanese operations, giving it greater freedom to develop the brand's distinctly Japanese identity. From there, the chain continued to expand, eventually bringing its donuts to markets including Thailand, Australia, Taiwan, and Singapore. Today, Mister Donut is best known for its playful, distinctly Japanese creations, particularly the Pon De Ring, a chewy, ring-shaped donut made up of small dough balls, and Mocchurin, its mochi-inspired donut line that is so soft, they require paper trays to keep each donut from losing its shape.

    Skip Tortilla Chips: Make Totchos For 10x The Flavor & Texture

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (511 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The appeal of nachos is easy to understand: Cover tortilla chips with a variable mix of cheese, meat, and beans, and dig into a mouth-watering textural experience.
    • It has been revealed that at first glance, it may seem like potatoes and nacho toppings shouldn't go together; tots are often a breakfast dish, after all.
    • So layer on ingredients like gooey cheese, corn and beans, flavorful ground meat or chorizo, salsa, pickled jalapeños, and more.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The appeal of nachos is easy to understand: Cover tortilla chips with a variable mix of cheese, meat, and beans, and dig into a mouth-watering textural experience. It's a dish concept that originated in Mexico, but it has since become widely popularized in the USA, welcoming many modifications in the process. Want a version with a thick boost in flavor and texture? Make a batch of totchos, swapping the tortilla chips for miniature hash browns (aka tater tots).

    It has been revealed that at first glance, it may seem like potatoes and nacho toppings shouldn't go together; tots are often a breakfast dish, after all. Yet the spuds make for an excellent starchy flavor canvas, ready for whatever nacho fixings you throw on. Like other loaded tater tot recipes, it's all about contrasting flavors atop a canvas of crispy potatoes.

    So layer on ingredients like gooey cheese, corn and beans, flavorful ground meat or chorizo, salsa, pickled jalapeños, and more. Some bites will get a little wet, but most will remain crunchy. Yet since tater tots are much thicker than chips, the underside retains a sturdy foundation, propping up a nacho twist with a little more heft. It's among the most delicious hacks for a bag of frozen tater tots, meshing together a freezer classic item with a crowd favorite formula.

    According to recent reports, A platter of totchos fits a variety of contexts. Layer on an abundance of festive components, and the dish can be an all-out party platter. Keep it to a simple meat and cheese, and you get an affordable and comforting rendition. Whichever route you go for, construct the dish with a few considerations in mind to optimize both flavor and texture.

    When preparing the tater tots, aim for peak crunch, so cook them well before you add your toppings. A hot oven gets the job done, but consider also using the air fryer for restaurant-level crunch, or even pan-frying the tots — maybe even in chorizo fat for added flavor. Next in importance is how to incorporate the dairy, another nacho cornerstone.

    Recent findings suggest that if you're making a liquidy nacho cheese sauce, you can simply drizzle the condiment onto your tots. However, if you're using shredded cheese, you'll want to melt the component on top of the tots in the oven for around five minutes. During this step, you can include already prepped ground beef taco meat, too, melding the dish components alongside the bed of potatoes.

    Industry observers note that only right before serving should you include cold ingredients. Keep it simple with chopped lettuce and onions, a light drizzle of sour cream or crema, or consider something more complex, like pico de gallo and guacamole. Cilantro and scallions are always welcome, as is a squeeze of lime. Dig in with a fork and knife (and we do suggest using cutlery — unlike with chips, you won't be easily able to grab individual tots); totchos's hearty appeal is immediate — it's the magic of nachos, with a heftier base.

    It has been revealed that there's hardly a saying that expresses unbridled joy like "kid in a candy store." But why do kids get all the fun? Candy stores, those brightly colored meccas of sky-high sugar intake, beckon many Americans far into adulthood. Candy, after all, is one of those food products that can really take us back, so candy stores are capable of injecting a sense of nostalgia, childlike reverie, and excitement into anyone's day.

    Candy has long been a staple of American culture, with the oldest candy stores in the United States stretching back into past centuries. In the modern world, however, candy enthusiasts keep tabs on their favorite indulgences through candy-focused blogs, sweets-obsessed Instagram accounts, and TikTok viral candy sensations. Meanwhile, towns, states, and even nationwide publications regularly hold contests for the best candy store in the area (or in the country). These sources, and more, inspired this list of the coolest candy stores in the United States.

    Sources indicate that and in a society where more is more, candy stores have evolved from quaint little shops (still worth a visit for transporting yourself to the past) to mega-sized outlets overflowing with sweets. Some have blossomed into department store-level or warehouse-like square footage, others have added attractions far beyond the candy itself, from mini golf to candy museums, and some are just old-time-tastic. The candy stores listed here are not just the perfect places to get your candy fix. They've become must-visit destinations for travelers around the country.

    According to recent reports, philadelphia's Shane Confectionery is one of America's oldest candy stores — in fact, it's the oldest continuously operated confectionery. The company emphasizes that this claim to fame means that its operation has been consistently making and selling confections longer than any other site in America, in a historic four-story brick building that's survived for over 150 years.

    Industry observers note that but it wasn't until 1910, when the tech giant was sold to Edward R. Shane, that many of the retail shop's intricate, old-fashioned design elements were put into place. As the company explains, Shane installed elaborately carved cabinets, curved glass showcases, and marble countertops to highlight his confections, as well as stained glass transom windows above the storefront to allure passersby in front of his shop. Best of all, many of these architectural details have been restored and are on display in the shop today, making a visit there a bit like stepping into a charming bygone era.

    It's no wonder that Eater Philadelphia has called Shane Confectionery the "time portal to Philadelphia's sugary past," calling out the efforts of current owners, brothers Ryan and Eric Berley, who breathed new life into the longstanding business in 2011. Fans regularly show it love online as a must-visit when living in or traveling through the City of Brotherly Love.

    110 Market St, Philadelphia, PA 19106.

    Industry observers note that with enthusiastic reviews and a high rankings online, Sweet Pete's Candy in Jacksonville, Florida, is hailed as the largest candy store in the Southeast. And the setting can't be beat: Visit Jacksonville points out that it's located in a historic 22,000-square-foot mansion right in the heart of downtown. From sour candies to hand-pulled lollipops, Sweet Pete's has your candy cravings covered.

    Sweet Pete's Candy also gets a leg up on the candy competition by serving customers with dietary restrictions. It offers an entire allergy-friendly array of candies, including a selection of gluten-free, dairy-free, vegan-friendly, and nut-free options. A classic treat is Pete's Famous Sea Salt Caramel, now available in different flavors, like Apple Pie.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, visitors can make a day out of their visit, because Sweet Pete's also houses Fizzies & Fare, an in-house restaurant and bar that's touted by the manufacturer as home to hundreds of unique craft sodas, over-the-top Crazy Shakes, classic American eats, candy-inspired cocktails, and more. Candy fans can also learn how their favorite candies are made through a guided tour, led by one of the staff's "Candy Connoisseurs," through the three-story "candy mansion," then grab their own handmade custom chocolate bar fresh from Sweet Pete's kitchen. The business even hosts parties, events, field trips for local school kids, and classes on-site.

    400 N Hogan St, Jacksonville, FL 32202.

    Sweet Mickey's, in the Ballard neighborhood of Seattle, is named after owner Randy Brinker's grandma and pays homage to her bygone party shop and homemade sweets. Many publications laud it as one of the best candy stores in the country, thanks to its variety of homemade fudges and truffles alongside classic candy favorites like Sugar Babies and international sensations like Danish salted licorice.

    Industry observers note that with a storefront tucked into the charming brick buildings of historic Ballard, it's the perfect place for a candy store with a vintage vibe and an old-time Americana aesthetic. From handmade goodies to its carefully curated selection of traditional and artisanal sweets from around the globe, candy lovers (or even the pickiest of eaters) can find something for them.

    Even better, this candy store has a heart. Since its 2012 grand opening, it has supported the local Little League, sponsored movie nights in the park, and hosted onsite parties and events to create sweet memories and build community.

    5338 Ballard Ave NW, Seattle, WA 98107.

    Recent findings suggest that it'Sugar, with candy-colored locations nationwide, was already known for its San Francisco flagship location, with a three-floor candy store in Fisherman's Wharf. The brand, with locations from coast to coast, then opened a 24,000-square-foot location in East Rutherford, New Jersey's American Dream shopping mall. This location, dubbed the World's First Candy Department Store, also spans three floors, though there are plenty across the country.

    Some of its over-the-top features at the East Rutherford location include: a three-story-tall Statue of Liberty replica covered in more than 1.5 million Jelly Belly beans, an immersive lollipop garden filled with nearly 10,000 lollipops, dozens of branded shops like Sour Patch Kids, Swedish Fish, Nerds, Starburst, and Reese's. It's truly a candy lover's dream come true. YouTubers have hailed it as an amazing feat of candy awesomeness, all a stone's throw from Fresh York City.

    The brand It'Sugar calls itself a "retailtainer," a mashup of retailer and entertainment. As company lore explains, the brand was founded by candy veteran Jeff Rubin in 2006 and has grown to more than 120 locations throughout the United States and Canada. It's known for "absurd sugar innovations" and the Sugar High Club, with which loyal visitors can earn points for their purchases — then, of course, they can cash them in for more sugar.

    It has been revealed that cleveland hosts North America's largest candy store, going strong for more than 75 years: b.a. Sweetie Candy Company. Cleveland.com calls it Cleveland's version of Willy Wonka's Candy Factory, and for good reason. Company stats boast that it hosts more than 500,000 visitors per year (making it one of the city's top attractions) and stocks more than 5,500 items in its wholesale store, to the tune of over $5 million in inventory on-hand at any given time.

    It has been revealed that with classic candy, retro candy, bulk candy, wholesale candy, and more, the store promises "the absolute largest variety of candy available anywhere in North America." Meaning, if you need 1,000 pounds of Tootsie Rolls to throw a parade, it's your outlet. It even keeps an eye on bygone favorites and claims it has been instrumental in bringing back vintage candies that had disappeared from shelves, including nostalgic names like Bonomo's Turkish Taffy, Slo Poke, Regal Crown, and Broadway licorice rolls.

    Industry observers note that all that would be enough to lure any candy fan, but b.a. Sweetie Candy Tech giant is much more than just a candy store. It's a bona fide family-fun destination, offering Golfland Park, which has two 18-hole mini golf courses, complete with lights for evening play, koi ponds, a cascading waterfall, and concession stands. Meanwhile, the Soda Shoppe serves up homemade ice cream, sundaes, malts, and over 100 sodas in a barn-style parlor.

    6770 Brookpark Rd, Cleveland, OH 44129.

    It has been revealed that this Latest York City treasure actually started as a shoe and hat repair shop — but a little push cart outside also sold candy. According to company lore, in the Depression years, 1937, the business owners decided to focus on their biggest moneymaker, candy, and became known as Economy Candy. After World War II, Morris "Moishe" Cohen and his brother in law assumed ownership and expanded the business, selling candy, chocolate, gift baskets, dried fruit, nuts, and more. Morris' son, Jerry, and his wife, Ilene, took over after its move to the current location at 108 Rivington Street, then passed the business to son Mitchell, who runs it today.

    In other words, this living legend is a true family affair — and a multigenerational sensation that has become a part of the rich history of Newly introduced York City. In 2023, the northwest corner of Rivington and Essex Streets were co-named Morris "Moishe" Cohen Way in honor of Morris and Economy Candy's lasting legacies.

    Today, the store still boasts over 2,000 items for sale, and visitors routinely rave about its massive selection and reasonable prices online. Hot sellers include chocolate-covered graham crackers (with and without jelly), chocolate-covered pretzels, jelly rings, gummies, and those hard-to-find candy bars. For those outside New York City, Economy Candy offers online sales, as well.

    108 Rivington St, Newly introduced York, NY 10002.

    Industry observers note that A candy shop with old-fashioned soda fountain treats like ice cream, specialty chocolate candies and fudge, more than 400 candies for buying in bulk, and 3,000-plus wrapped candies — all in colorful circus-theme surroundings? Yes, please.

    It has been revealed that the Substantial Top Candy Shop has been serving the Austin community (as well as candy-minded travelers) since 2007. Visitors praised its wall-to-wall candy selection, laid out in candy-colored rows, jars, racks, and even in a lollipop tree. Passing by Peanuts, the elephant pictured on the shop's entrance (facing the city's famed South Congress Avenue, known for housing quirky boutiques), visitors will find a whimsical wonderland at Big Top Candy with classic soda machines, retro candies, and a hefty bulk section customers can grab by the scoop.

    Industry observers note that the store promises both nostalgic favorites and new creations from around the globe. Whether you're just passing through for SXSW or a stalwart resident, Substantial Top Candy Shop is a must-visit in the Live Music Capital of the World.

    1706 S Congress Ave, Austin, TX 78704.

    Minnesota's Largest Candy Store in Jordan, Minnesota, nods to its mind-boggling mass of inventory in its very name — and the company would seem intent on living up to that moniker. Owned by Robert Wagner, and also known as Jim's Apple Farm, the store houses not only nostalgic candy, but fresh-baked pies and strudels, the world's largest selection of sodas, an array of popcorn flavors, and locally-sourced items (think pastas, jams, jellies, and even puzzles). These are all sourced from surrounding farms, making this Midwestern gem not only a candy emporium but a true shopping destination that supports locals and promotes Minnesota products to everyone who enters.

    Recent findings suggest that fortunately, its location is relatively convenient for passers-through, as the store is only 35 miles from Minneapolis. And you can't miss it — the store is housed in a massive, bright yellow barn. It's a must-stop not only thanks to its dizzying array of sweet and savory treats, but fun touches throughout its interior decor, such as a fresh observatory-like dome featuring a mural with more than two dozen superheroes, an animatronic band, and a fortune-telling machine. Essentially, this Minnesota behemoth will bring out the kid in anyone.

    minnesotaslargestcandystore.com.

    20430 Johnson Memorial Dr, Jordan, MN 55352.

    It has been revealed that calling itself one of the oldest continuously operated, family-owned candy businesses in the U.S., Schimpff's Confectionery has been hailed as America's best candy store. It was also featured on a national television special "Disney Celebrates America: The Pursuit of Happiness.".

    Sources indicate that with 135 years of history, Schimpff's Confectionery more than deserves those honors — its recipes and business stretch back to the 1800s. The company history notes that the recipe for its famous Cinnamon Red Hots were handwritten in the recipe book of Gustav "Gus" Schimpff Sr. back in 1891. And it's still making waves, having been featured on several reveals and publications.

    In a recent development, with such an illustrious history, it makes sense that Schimpff's Confectionery also houses a candy museum, with thousands of pieces of American candy memorabilia. The museum, along with a candy demonstration area, were added to an adjacent building in 2001, a dream child of 1990s-era owners Warren Schimpff and his wife Jill. Today, fifth-generation owners Steve and Beth Shepherd have taken the helm and embrace the time-honored traditions and recipes at Schimpff's Confectionery.

    347 Spring St, Jeffersonville, IN 47130.

    In a recent development, seeking candy from the 1970s, or maybe your favorite candy from the 1990s? The Peppermint Stick Candy Store & Ice Cream Parlor in Boyertown, Pennsylvania, stocks a cornucopia of vintage candies alongside modern-day favorites and gourmet goodies like truffles. Whether you're visiting in-store or shopping online, this candy store has got you covered. In fact, its website has a handy online shopping feature, making it easy for customers to browse by decade.

    Industry observers note that opened in 2015, this woman-owned business also offers Longacre's ice cream for indulgent sundaes and 20-ounce milkshakes, plus bakery delights like Ice Cream Nachos (waffle cones make the chips) and the Cinnamon Roll Sundae, and a Soda Jerk menu with soda fountain favorites. Customers will find not just a store, but an unforgettable experience at The Peppermint Stick Candy Store & Ice Cream Parlor. They can find fudge, artisan chocolates, loose chocolates, gummy candy, penny candy, nostalgic candy, gourmet truffles (in flavors like mint, Champagne, tiramisu, and key lime), and even a penny candy section. Basically, if you leave hungry, you've done something wrong.

    26 E Philadelphia Ave, Boyertown, PA 19512.

    Since 1934, Bright's Candies has been whipping up candy the old-fashioned way. Even now, this destination features charming equipment to make its treats, including large copper kettles, metal candy molds, and an antique popcorn popper in its candy kitchen. Even better, the viewing windows in the shop are designed to give everyone a front row look at the process, allowing kids and adults to watch the staff confectioners at work. All of these factors contribute to an impressively high Yelp rating, where customers called it cute and charming, with a heavenly smell and friendly staff members.

    This candy store won national recognition for its sweet treats, and for decades, has been known for wafting aromas of caramel corn and waffle cones down Walla Walla's Main Street. Try out the chocolates, truffles, and seasonal items like handmade chocolate Easter bunnies. Or, go for fudge, licorice, or colorful frozen treats. In other words, it's not just a candy store; it's a place to immerse all of your senses in sweets. What's not to love about that?

    11 E Main St, Walla Walla, WA 99362.

    This list was compiled using review sites like Reddit, Google, and Tripadvisor; research on candy stores' websites from coast to coast; and tracking media mentions on major news outlets. Extra attention was given to candy stores that are historic and/or boast unique offerings to visitors, such as mini golf, soda fountains, museums, and more.
